data.narrative:
Radical AI is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $55M to date. The company operates within a sector comprising one public comparable and eight private peers, including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Bedrock Robotics. The founding team combines deep technical expertise—CEO Joseph Krause brings neuromorphic semiconductor research from the Army Research Lab and prior deep-tech investing experience; CSO Prof. Gerbrand Ceder is a UC Berkeley materials science professor with 25 years in academia.

Given the company's seed stage and lack of sufficient near-peer comparables at identical stage and valuation tier, peer-median analysis is not applicable; a broader sector median would introduce unacceptable noise. Accordingly, stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable triangulation approach. Using the $55M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a typical 2.5x multiplier for seed-to-next-stage advancement yields $138M.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $117M to $158M, centered on $138M. Key uncertainties include the absence of granular financial performance data (revenue, burn rate, unit economics), the narrow applicability of stage-progression as a sole method, and limited comparability within the robotics sector at this stage. A fuller valuation would benefit from revenue-based or DCF methods as the company matures operationally.
